_comment: Hand-verified license readings, keyed by repo slug. GitHub's API collapses every license it cannot identify into spdx_id NOASSERTION (name 'Other'), so a source-available license and a bespoke permissive one look identical in the metadata. Where we opened the license file ourselves, the real terms are recorded here. Since data/stack.json records OBSERVED Stack v3 membership, these readings explain a verdict rather than decide it; `stack_eligible` remains as the forward-looking call for the next snapshot and as the fallback when a repo has no observed answer.

basecamp/fizzy.note: MIT-style grant plus a clause forbidding use as a competing hosted/SaaS product, so it is not permissive. Went public 2025-12-02, after the Stack v3 crawl cutoff (2025-08-07), so its absence from v3 is timing; the license would keep its files out of the permissive set in the next snapshot regardless.

rubygems/guides.note: README: article content is CC, example code is MIT. GitHub cannot match the CCPL text, hence NOASSERTION, and share-alike terms make file-level keeping a judgment call only the corpus itself can settle.

karafka/wiki.actual: custom, 'All Rights Reserved' for original wiki content
karafka/wiki.note: Original content is all-rights-reserved with permitted non-commercial use; third-party content (librdkafka, Kafka docs) is carved out under its own terms. By the text this is non-permissive; the v3 file-level scanner evidently read it differently, which is exactly why the observed answer outranks the reading.
